p.i: Numquam eadem, similisque sibi sub sole videtur Pluma leuis, modo purpureo fulgere piropo, Nunc virides auro credas circundare gemmas, Spectantumque oculos dubia sub imagine ludit. Sub pedibus natura, & inobseruabile fatum, Quaeque leues hominum mentes fortuna fatigat, Bisseni circum radij canentia cingunt Tempora, non ipsi diuinae spicula lucis Coelicolae sufferre valent, non ora tueri Comminus, oppositisque obnubunt lumina pennis. Vt Pater omnipotens tanto in discrimine classem Esse videt, monstrumque Erebi venisse sub auras, Iamque odijs versare rates, iam crimina belli Inferere, & placidas furijs accendere mentes, Communemque legit coelestum in fronte dolorem, Annuit, & puerum iubet ocyus aethere labi Vnum ex alitibus, fessasque accedere naues, Vt tandem ponti longis erroribus actae Speratos tangant portus, non cepta retardet Aut metas, aut inuisa fames, non foeta dolis gens Missa Erebo, placidi subsidant marmoris irae, Et lux optatas ostendit crastina terras Sic fixum est, summiquePatris haec certa voluntas. Ille volat, nitido perfusum lumine coelum Risit, & obstantes penitus cessere tenebrae, Pictaque non solita tremuerunt aequora luce. Forte Duci ferus labentia lumina somnus

page.notes: The verse is printed in italic throughout; the stanza breaks are not marked, so the poem is given as one paragraph with its lines kept. The word "Pictaque" has an unusual P with a flourish, read as P. The final line of the poem is indented on the page. The catchword "Pressera" is set italic at the lower right.
